comments.body: Can you add a test that check that passing `['indexA', 'indexB']` (ie. not array of objects) should fail, as expected?

> Can you add a test that check that passing ['indexA', 'indexB'](ie. not array of objects) should fail, as expected?

I think that's really related to https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/issues/309#issuecomment-149864298 => tldr; I don't think we want to re-implement all checks React is providing in dev :/
I will add a test checking that we correctly send back an error if there is no attribute `name` in the object.

My point was not about re-testing the correct props. I agree that we should use the tooling we already have.

My point was that we had a test that was passing when it should have failed. So now that we are fixing it, we should add a test, to make sure we do not introduce any regression later, like for any other feature.

I agree with you @pixelastic , except in the case where we're not respecting our own documentation (which we weren't). But having a larger test that will at the same time cover is a good solution IMHO.
Yep, makes sense, we were not even following our own documentation here, so bugs were expected. I agree the test I was suggesting is not really needed.

title: fix(index-selector): Fix tests passing with incorrect parameters
